videos.title: VoiceOver sigue abriendo puertas. Phonon trae nuevas voces a la conversación
videos.description:
VoiceOver continúa ampliando sus posibilidades, y hoy le toca el turno a Phonon, una aplicación que permite incorporar nuevas voces al lector de pantalla de Apple.
En este tutorial conoceremos cómo funciona Phonon, cómo explorar las voces disponibles, seleccionar las que nos interesan, descargarlas y utilizarlas con VoiceOver.
Todo explicado paso a paso, con demostraciones prácticas para que puedan escuchar las voces y valorar cuáles se ajustan mejor a sus preferencias.
Porque cuando hablamos de accesibilidad, tener más opciones para elegir siempre es una buena noticia.

videos.title: ¿Una galería de fotos pensada para personas ciegas? Así funciona Memora
videos.description:
Memora: ¿para qué quiere una persona ciega una galería de fotos?
¿Quién dijo que las fotografías son solamente para quienes pueden verlas?
Hoy les presento Memora, una aplicación para iPhone desarrollada por un programador ciego que propone una forma accesible de explorar y organizar nuestras fotografías.
En este tutorial recorreremos sus principales funciones, comprobaremos cómo se maneja con VoiceOver y veremos qué posibilidades ofrece en la práctica.
Una nueva oportunidad para demostrar que la accesibilidad también tiene mucho que decir en el mundo de la fotografía.
TifloAcosta. Tecnología al alcance de todos.

videos.title: Apple te quiere… proteger. ¡Pero tienes que activarlo! iOS 27
videos.description:
Apple quiere protegernos de las estafas, y con iOS 27 incorpora una nueva función llamada «Detección de riesgo de suplantación de identidad».
¿En qué consiste? ¿Puede nuestro iPhone detectar que alguien está intentando engañarnos para conseguir nuestro dinero o nuestros datos personales?
En este vídeo de TifloAcosta explico cómo funciona esta protección, cuáles son sus limitaciones y cómo podemos activarla desde los ajustes del iPhone utilizando VoiceOver.
Una novedad importante que viene desactivada de fábrica y que necesita aplicaciones compatibles para funcionar. No evita todas las estafas, pero puede aportar una protección adicional.

videos.title: Yo ya no persigo las noticias: ahora vienen a buscarme
videos.description:
En este vídeo les presento cMRSS, una aplicación accesible que permite reunir en un mismo lugar las fuentes de noticias y contenidos que realmente nos
interesan.
Podemos añadir medios y páginas mediante sus fuentes RSS, organizar lo que seguimos y consultar las novedades sin tener que ir saltando de una web a otra.
Pero hay una función que a mí me ha gustado especialmente: también podemos añadir canales de YouTube y seguir sus nuevas publicaciones desde la propia
aplicación, sin necesidad de entrar continuamente en YouTube para comprobar qué han publicado.
cMRSS no es gratuita, y eso también hay que decirlo. Pero después de usarla y comprobar lo que me ofrece, en mi caso considero que merece la pena la inversión.
En el vídeo les enseño cómo funciona, qué posibilidades ofrece y por qué se ha ganado un sitio entre las aplicaciones que utilizo para mantenerme informado.

videos.title: TifloAcosta ya tiene app: todo cambia a partir de aquí
videos.description:
TIFLOACOSTA APP — ACCESO DIRECTO
Este enlace abre directamente TifloAcosta App. No necesitas descargar ningún archivo ni registrarte para entrar. Desde ahí puedes utilizar la aplicación en el navegador y, si quieres, instalarla en tu dispositivo para tenerla disponible como una app más.
TifloAcosta da hoy uno de los pasos más importantes desde que comenzó este proyecto.
Durante mucho tiempo hemos ido creando vídeos, cursos, guías, documentos, recursos en español y en inglés y una comunidad que sigue creciendo. El problema es que todo ese material estaba repartido entre distintos lugares.
Ha llegado el momento de empezar a reunirlo.
TifloAcosta ya tiene su propia app.
Desde ella puedes buscar recursos por palabras, recorrerlos por categorías, consultar las novedades, guardar tus favoritos y acceder al catálogo completo de vídeos del Canal TifloAcosta.
Además, la aplicación se ha pensado desde el principio teniendo en cuenta la accesibilidad y el uso con lectores de pantalla.
En este vídeo te enseño cómo funciona, qué puedes encontrar dentro y cómo puedes instalarla para tener TifloAcosta mucho más cerca.
La demostración práctica se realiza en iPhone utilizando VoiceOver, y también explico cómo acceder e instalarla desde Android y Windows.
Si quieres entrar directamente mientras ves el vídeo, este es nuevamente el enlace:
La aplicación seguirá creciendo.
Iremos incorporando nuevos recursos, mejorando lo que ya existe y ajustando aquello que la experiencia real de los usuarios nos vaya indicando.
Porque esto no pretende ser simplemente otra página donde acumular enlaces.
La idea es mucho más ambiciosa: crear un lugar estable, accesible y sencillo desde el que entrar a todo lo que TifloAcosta va construyendo.
Hasta ahora, TifloAcosta era principalmente un canal, una comunidad y una colección de contenidos repartidos por distintos espacios.
Desde hoy empieza a tener su propia casa.
Y acabamos de abrir la puerta.

videos.title: Este atajo no pregunta, ve un código y se pone a investigar
videos.description:
Ponle un código delante… y a ver qué pasa
Hoy les traigo uno de esos atajos que empiezas haciendo para resolver una cosa y al final termina haciendo bastante más de lo previsto.
La idea es sencilla: encontrar un código y averiguar qué contiene.
Puede trabajar con códigos que estén en una imagen o una captura guardada en el iPhone, pero también con códigos que tengamos delante y podamos captar con la cámara.
Y no nos quedamos únicamente con los códigos QR.
El atajo también puede reconocer códigos de barras y, cuando encuentra información que merece la pena investigar, utiliza Internet para intentar averiguar qué hay detrás de ese código y ofrecernos información útil.
Por ejemplo, podemos encontrarnos un código de barras en un producto y querer saber qué es, o recibir una imagen que contiene un QR sin tener otro teléfono disponible para escanearlo.
La intención ha sido precisamente esa: tener una herramienta sencilla y accesible que podamos lanzar desde el iPhone y dejar que haga el trabajo.
En el vídeo les enseño cómo funciona y las distintas posibilidades que ofrece.
IMPORTANTE:
Para utilizar este atajo es necesario tener instalada la aplicación gratuita Actions, ya que algunas de las funciones que utiliza el atajo proceden de esta aplicación.
Descargar Actions desde la App Store:
Instalar el atajo:
Una vez instalada Actions, conviene abrirla al menos una vez. Si sus acciones no aparecen posteriormente en la aplicación Atajos, reinicien el iPhone.
Como siempre, este atajo lo comparto para que puedan probarlo, jugar con él y, sobre todo, sacarle partido.
Tony Acosta
Canal TifloAcosta

El atajo también puede reconocer códigos de barras y, cuando encuentra información que merece la pena investigar, utiliza Internet para intentar averiguar qué hay detrás de ese código y ofrecernos información útil.

Por ejemplo, podemos encontrarnos un código de barras en un producto y querer saber qué es, o recibir una imagen que contiene un QR sin tener otro teléfono disponible para escanearlo.

La intención ha sido precisamente esa: tener una herramienta sencilla y accesible que podamos lanzar desde el iPhone y dejar que haga el trabajo.

En el vídeo les enseño cómo funciona y las distintas posibilidades que ofrece.

IMPORTANTE:

Para utilizar este atajo es necesario tener instalada la aplicación gratuita Actions, ya que algunas de las funciones que utiliza el atajo proceden de esta aplicación.

https://apps.apple.com/es/app/actions/id1586435171

Instalar el atajo:
https://www.icloud.com/shortcuts/477bfbed55a84c1aa568b748acd638de

Una vez instalada Actions, conviene abrirla al menos una vez. Si sus acciones no aparecen posteriormente en la aplicación Atajos, reinicien el iPhone.

Como siempre, este atajo lo comparto para que puedan probarlo, jugar con él y, sobre todo, sacarle partido.

videos.title: Actualizaciones invisibles en iPhone: qué son y por qué importan
videos.description:
Apple no solo actualiza el iPhone cuando aparece una nueva versión de iOS. Existe un sistema menos visible que trabaja en segundo plano y que mucha gente no conoce: las actualizaciones rápidas de seguridad y datos del sistema.
Estas actualizaciones no requieren descargar una versión completa del sistema ni reiniciar el dispositivo. Se aplican de forma automática y están diseñadas para corregir fallos de seguridad urgentes, actualizar bases de datos internas o mejorar el funcionamiento de servicios clave.
Se encuentran dentro de Ajustes, General, Actualización de software, y dependen de una opción llamada “Respuestas de seguridad y archivos del sistema”. Si está activada, el iPhone puede recibir mejoras sin que el usuario tenga que hacer nada.
En este vídeo se explica qué son exactamente estas actualizaciones, qué cambian en el dispositivo, por qué Apple las utiliza cada vez más y qué ventajas tienen frente a las actualizaciones tradicionales de iOS.
videos.fullDescription:

news.title: TurnOver
news.summary: TurnOver is a free, open-source screen reader for the Mac that works alongside VoiceOver. It sits in the menu bar and takes over from VoiceOver in the apps you choose, such as Mail, Safari, Terminal, and Microsoft Word. Much of its design comes from NVDA, with browse mode for web pages and email, single-letter quick navigation, find, say all, and an elements list. It also understands VoiceOver's own commands. Switch to any other app and VoiceOver comes straight back.

news.title: South Korea proceeds with case over allegedly misleading Apple Intelligence ads
news.summary: South Korea’s Fair Trade Commission (KFTC) announced today that it has opened formal proceedings against Apple over its advertising of Apple Intelligence features for the iPhone 16 lineup. Here are the details. more…
news.body:
South Korea’s Fair Trade Commission (KFTC) announced today that it has opened formal proceedings against Apple over its advertising of Apple Intelligence features for the iPhone 16 lineup. Here are the details.

Back in March 2025, shortly after Apple announced it was delaying the rollout of what would eventually become Siri AI, the South Korean civic group Seoul YMCA filed a complaint with the KFTC.

At the time, Yonhap reported that the organization had previously called on Apple to compensate affected customers, and alleged that the company may have continued to market the iPhone 16 lineup despite already knowing that some of its advertised AI features would be delayed.

As 9to5Mac readers will likely remember, Apple widely advertised Apple Intelligence and AI-powered Siri features as part of its iPhone 16 launch campaign, going so far as to give its iconic Fifth Avenue store an Apple Intelligence-themed makeover and run an ad campaign starring Bella Ramsey.

This landed Apple in legal and regulatory trouble in multiple markets, including the US, where the company agreed to a $250 million class action settlement earlier this year, and Brazil , where it came under scrutiny from a consumer protection agency in May. Now, the company is facing potential penalties in South Korea as well.

As a result of Seoul YMCA’s complaint, the KFTC conducted an investigation into Apple’s advertising practices. Today, the regulator announced (via MacRumors ) that its investigators had submitted their findings and recommendations for formal deliberation by the Commission.

According to the KFTC’s press release, investigators concluded that Apple advertised Apple Intelligence and its planned staggered rollout on the iPhone 16 website, but “concealed, downplayed, or omitted information material to consumers’ purchasing decisions.”

That included, per the press release (translation ours):

The press release also notes that Genmoji, Image Playground, “Siri with the ability to understand personal context,” and “Siri that provides step-by-step guidance” were not made available as advertised:

For example, Siri’s ability to understand personal context was advertised as being scheduled to launch first in US English by the end of 2024, as currently available in US English in October 2024, and as scheduled to support Korean in early April 2025.

In reality, the feature was not launched in US English until September 2026, with Korean language support following in October 2026.

As a result, the investigators concluded that Apple’s conduct constituted a violation of the country’s Labeling and Advertising Act, which prohibits deceptive labeling and advertising.

They recommended issuing corrective orders, including a prohibition on such conduct in the future, as well as imposing a financial penalty.

They also estimate that Apple’s revenue associated with the alleged violation amounts to approximately 3.35 trillion South Korean won (roughly $2.5 billion), though the KFTC’s press release does not specify the amount of the fine.

⁠ Yonhap noted today that the fine could reach roughly $48 million, while ⁠ KBS reported that it could range between $21 million and $42 million.

With the report now submitted, Apple has six weeks to submit its written defense before the Commission deliberates and makes a final determination on whether the company violated the law and, if so, how much it should be fined.

In a statement to MacRumors , Apple said it had cooperated with the KFTC’s investigation, but disagreed with the conclusions. The company also highlighted the rollout of Korean-language support for Apple Intelligence last year and, more recently, for Siri AI.

For the original press release, follow this link .

news.title: Readdle’s Documents app adds voice recording with transcripts, summaries, more
news.summary: Readdle updated its Documents app for iPhone and iPad this week with Voice Notes, a new AI-powered feature that lets users record conversations and automatically generate transcripts, summaries, and follow-up notes. Here are the details. more…
news.body:
Readdle updated its Documents app for iPhone and iPad this week with Voice Notes, a new AI-powered feature that lets users record conversations and automatically generate transcripts, summaries, and follow-up notes. Here are the details.

While the habit of recording meetings, lectures, or even one’s own thoughts is not particularly new, modern AI tools and models have made it considerably easier to extract useful information from these recordings without having to listen back to them in their entirety or take copious notes that can distract from the actual conversation.

This week, Readdle’s Documents introduced Voice Notes, which “lets you record audio and turn it into a summary, follow-ups, and a full transcript,” as the company put it.

Users can start a new recording session by tapping the “+” button in the app and selecting Voice Notes. Alternatively, they can start recording from the iPhone’s Action button, which is a nice touch.

Once they’re done, Readdle says Documents can generate:

Users can cycle through these three tabs, where they can also listen to the original recording or copy and share the information.

Readdle says Voice Notes can recognize multiple languages in the same conversation, with the actual transcript preserving the languages as spoken, “while the summary and follow-ups are generated in the most frequently spoken language.”

Each voice note is saved as a single file in Documents that contains the original recording, transcript, summary, and follow-ups. Users can organize these files into folders, share them, sync them with their cloud storage, and save the transcript as a separate .txt file.

For more privacy-conscious users, the platform’s privacy policy states that the company doesn’t ordinarily retain Voice Notes audio recordings, while the resulting transcripts and summaries are stored for up to an hour.

However, if users give a voice note’s AI-generated content a thumbs down, Readdle may retain its transcript and summary for up to six months, or until the user objects to their processing, whichever comes first.

The company also says user data isn’t used to train AI models, although third-party AI providers may retain inputs for up to 30 days for abuse and misuse monitoring, or longer if required by law.

Voice Notes is available to Documents Plus subscribers at no additional cost and with unlimited recording minutes. New subscribers can try the service for free for seven days.

To learn more about Voice Notes in Documents, follow this link .

news.title: Nvidia hits pause on chip shipments to Southeast Asia
news.summary: Nvidia has told manufacturing partners to pause server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia as the U.S. tightens its push to keep AI chips out of China.
news.body:
Posted:

Nvidia is under pressure to do things differently, and a new WSJ report shows how far that’s going.

According to the Journal, Nvidia has told manufacturing partners, including Dell and Super Micro, to hit pause on server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia for an unspecified period as it assesses whether its regional partners are meeting U.S. export requirements.

As for why those countries, Chinese companies have been tapping Nvidia chips remotely from data centers there, a loophole the US Commerce Department closed — reportedly grudgingly — earlier this month. The Journal notes that the think tank Institute for Progress estimates remote data centers like these supply about 24% of China’s AI computing power.

news.title: The Garmin Forerunner 265S is down to $300, its best price of the year
news.summary: The Forerunner 265S may not be the newest or flashiest Garmin, but it’s one that I’ve always loved most in testing. For runners with smaller wrists, it fits nicely. The battery life is pretty good thanks in part to its OLED touchscreen. When I reviewed it a few years ago, I called it the Goldilocks […]
news.body:
The Forerunner 265S may not be the newest or flashiest Garmin, but it’s one that I’ve always loved most in testing. For runners with smaller wrists, it fits nicely. The battery life is pretty good thanks in part to its OLED touchscreen. When I reviewed it a few years ago, I called it the Goldilocks of fitness watches at the time, and the only thing that bugged me was its price. But now that it’s down to $299.99 (a $150 discount off its MSRP) at Amazon and Best Buy for Black Friday, I can easily recommend it.

The neat thing about Garmins in general is that you really don’t need the latest models to get the most out of the company’s platform. Its watches tend to get firmware updates for several years after launch, which is how long the average Garmin user tends to hold on to theirs. This particular watch is best suited for folks who want something a bit slimmer and smaller, enjoy a pop of color, and want a little extra fitness tracking prowess — but don’t need the whole kit and caboodle that sends the price up by hundreds.

news.title: NVIDIA reportedly halts AI chip shipments to Southeast Asia
news.summary: In the same week that NVIDIA reinstated Jensen Huang as its CEO, the company has reportedly also blocked shipments to Southeast Asia.
news.body:
Companies like Dell have stopped shipping server hardware to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia.

NVIDIA has reportedly put a stop to shipments of AI server hardware to four Southeast Asian countries. According to The Financial Times , a handful of the company's manufacturing partners, including Dell and Supermicro, told clients in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia that the chipmaker is not allowing their server orders to be sent to them. The Financial Times reports it's unclear if the halt is temporary. The news comes just days after NVIDIA reinstated Jensen Huang as its chief executive .

In recent years, Chinese AI labs have turned to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia to gain access to NVIDIA's most powerful chips. They used a gap in US export controls by renting access through cloud compute providers that bought servers with NVIDIA GPUs inside. In recent weeks, the US Commerce Department moved to close that loophole. First by introducing new rules aimed at stopping that exact practice, and second by targeting Megaspeed, the company at the center of the NVIDIA scandal.

On Wednesday, the Commerce Department added Megaspeed to its "Entity List." Companies, including NVIDIA, now need a US license to ship goods covered by US export rules to Megaspeed. Huang had resigned from his position on November 12 after reports surfaced that he had engaged in multiple extramarital affairs, including one involving Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive that some US officials suspect was a Chinese intelligence asset . Megaspeed had leased access to NVIDIA chips to Chinese companies. The Justice Department is also investigating whether Megaspeed broke US export rules .

Under the new US rule, data centers that were already providing large amounts of computing power to companies based in China or other location covered by the rule have 90 days from November 19 to get a license if they want to keep doing so. "There's this new rule but no guidance on execution," one cloud executive told the outlet. "No one knows how to apply for this license while the 90-day clock is ticking. It's causing sheer chaos in the region." Demand from Chinese tech companies led to a data center construction boom in Southeast Asia. NVIDIA booked $104 billion in revenue through its Singapore subsidiary in 2025, representing a 72 percent increase from the year before.

news.title: A month with the iPhone Duo has changed how I use my phone
news.summary: From reading more books to breaking mindless scrolling habits, Apple's foldable has changed my daily routines in ways I didn't anticipate.
news.body:
For years, the definition of a premium smartphone depended on its cameras, processors, and how light it felt when you stowed it in your pocket. The iPhone Duo challenges that concept by asking consumers to pay more for a fundamentally different smartphone experience, even if it means sacrificing what they’ve long thought of as high-end features.

In a little under a month of using the Duo, I’ve found that the trade-offs I was initially concerned about matter far less to me than I had expected. What’s been more interesting is how the Duo’s foldable form factor has changed my everyday habits, including how I interact with apps, which apps I use, and how I organize and personalize the phone itself.

I also easily forgot a number of my initial concerns about switching to the Duo. The apps, for the most part, are now optimized for the Duo; I’ve reacquainted myself with Touch ID; and I don’t miss the Pro Max camera on most days.

That’s not to say the Duo doesn’t have its shortcomings. I still miss that telephoto lens sometimes, and I’m still longing for Face ID — though not as much since Apple shipped a face unlock feature in the latest update. But after a month of using the Duo, I’ve found these compromises have had less of an impact on my day-to-day experience compared with the benefits that the new form factor brings.

I was surprised by how much I’ve grown to appreciate the Duo’s multitasking capabilities. Initially, I didn’t think I’d regularly use it to view two apps side by side, given the still fairly limited screen space even while the phone is unfolded, especially compared with an iPad. But I’ve found myself snapping apps to both halves of the screen more often than I had imagined.

For starters, Apple has made this side-by-side mode incredibly intuitive and easy to use — you simply drag the app over to the left or right side of the screen and drop it into the target box that appears.

I have regularly taken advantage of this feature to do all sorts of things.

I really enjoy keeping X open as I read through the news, which allows me to switch back and forth between the article I’m reading and real-time reactions to it. Sometimes I’ll keep email or Slack open on the side while I’m working on something else so I don’t miss an important message or notification.

And much like the overstimulated members of Gen Z (which I am not), I sometimes like scrolling social media while engaging with some other media off to the side.

Case in point: I passively watched Netflix’s “Love is Blind” reunion while reading the gossipy tweets and Reddit posts about the main characters on the other side of the screen. This sort of TV watching behavior used to be called second-screen viewing , but now it’s morphing into something new. Everything is happening on one screen, so should we call it “Duo screen viewing,” perhaps? It makes me long for even more interactive TV experiences where commentary and content are combined.

I’ve noticed another shift in my behavior since adopting the Duo as my main device. When I’m out and about, the Duo feels more like an (arguably heavier) iPhone mini . For those who still miss smaller iPhones, the Duo is the next best thing. Despite its weight, the phone feels small. You can cover it with one hand; you can type with a thumb; you can reach the top and bottom easily; and you can even fit it into your front and back pockets. The Pro Max now feels unbelievably strange in my hand — how was I ever comfortable wrangling this giant rectangle?

The Duo’s small screen works well when you’re on the go, especially for short interactions like responding to a quick text or pulling up directions to a destination. It’s not as great for mindless scrolling, which I appreciate, as it forces me to engage with the real world instead of killing every moment of boredom or unease by opening up apps.

But when you’re home or somewhere with time to kill, you can unfold the screen and enjoy your apps super-sized. It’s the best of both worlds.

I find that I instinctively unfold the phone when I’m preparing to watch videos, because the larger screen is best for that. It’s also unfolded if I’m shopping, as it’s more convenient for looking at products, zooming in to examine the details, or complete checkout forms.

Generally, I also unfold the Duo when I’m actively using apps. This setup has also allowed me to rethink my Home Screen layout: With the Duo closed, I prefer to see just widgets on the small screen with key information like weather, time, battery life, and so on. Meanwhile, the only app icons on the Home Screen are those in the dock.

In the weeks since its launch, most of the apps that weren’t yet optimized for the Duo have been upgraded to support its foldable form factor. In mid-November, Apple said there were over 200,000 Duo-ready apps , and in my experience, that certainly feels true. A majority of my so-called “daily drivers” — with the glaring exception of key Google apps like Gmail and Drive — have dropped the black band on the side of the screen that was frustrating early testers of the phone.

Most apps now take advantage of the available space, whether that’s on the Duo’s small front screen or the wider, unfolded one.

I’ve also found it interesting to see the different interpretations developers have had for how to best optimize their app for Duo.

Some have used the form factor as a way to bring in some sort of novelty: there’s a note-taking app that opens and closes like a notebook , with pages you can write on with the Apple Pencil; a retro Walkman-like music player ; a tiny typewriter ; a gaming handheld ; a game where you close the phone to make grilled cheese .

As much as I love the whimsy of this group of apps, I appreciate how my everyday apps feel better to use on the unfolded screen. Spotify, at last, feels less cluttered when it has more screen real estate. A number of note-taking, list-making, and calendar apps also feel somehow more usable when spread out.

The Netflix app is actually fantastic with its support for multiple viewing modes, which include playing video on the closed outer display, the “laptop” orientation with its big player controls, and the “tent” mode.

Other developers have similarly reimagined how their app would work if it had originally been designed for the Duo’s small and larger screens.

One good example of this is Sofa, a handy utility for organizing the books, movies, TV shows, podcasts, albums, and games you want to check out. When the Duo is closed, its navigation is tucked off to the right side in a vertical bar, while the main screen focuses on the items you’ve saved. But when the Duo is unfolded, the number of items displayed on the screen also expands into a two-column layout, with more of your items featured on the screen and your lists on the left side. It doesn’t feel like two different apps, but like you’ve opened up the app itself and given it more space to spread out.

In terms of your daily social media scroll, apps like TikTok and Instagram have been updated to be perfectly usable on the Duo, whether the phone is open or closed. When closed, TikTok now stretches the video to cover the screen, instead of showing the ugly black bar. Scrolling short-form videos on the Duo, while unfolded like a slightly smaller iPad mini, has become my preferred way to watch.

Here’s another surprise: I’ve spent less time with my Kindle, and am instead reading books on my Duo. Unfolded, the Duo is a decent enough replacement for an e-book reader, albeit it can be a bit more stimulating as it’s not an e-ink device. However, the matte inner screen isn’t quite as bright and distracting as your typical glossy OLED display. There’s less glare and softer reflections, but there’s also something about the display that just feels calmer than a smartphone, allowing you to more fully engage with a book’s text.

Unfolded and held vertically, reading on the Duo feels a lot like reading on the standard Kindle, at least in terms of hand-feel. And putting your phone into the “Do Not Disturb” focus mode can help you not be distracted by incoming notifications and messages while you read.

You can also unfold the device while keeping it in landscape orientation, with the screens bent slightly inward like a real book. For even more fun, you can turn on Kindle’s page-turn animation, which makes it seem as if you’re turning the page in a physical book. And I love how you can “performatively read” using an app like Book2Life or Actually Read — they display the book’s cover on the Duo’s outer screen as you read the text on the inner screen.

E-book readers will likely find they can carry one less device when they’re out and about, because the Duo can stand in for whatever Kindle or other reader you typically keep in your purse or bag. You can save the Kindle for other times, whether that’s at home, on long travel days, or when you don’t want to worry about sand getting into your $2,000 phone.

On the big-screened iPhone 17 Pro Max I used to carry, I tended to keep a PopSocket of some sort on the back because the phone was both heavy and large, which made it hard to hold for longer periods of time. The Duo is similarly heavy, but its shape makes it far easier to hold in one hand without the extra help.

Folded, you can do the usual one-handed hold where the bottom edge of the phone rests on your pinky, your other three fingers cradle the back, and your thumb is free to navigate the screen.

Unfolded, the Duo’s like using a small Kindle or iPad mini, where two hands are required. You also don’t need a PopSocket for balancing the phone on the side, because it can be propped up like a tent or opened like a tiny laptop. Or, if you prefer, Apple and others offer Duo cases with a built-in stand. (Apple’s case comes in navy and taupe, though, so if you’re not boring, you’ll probably want to shop from third-party vendors).

If you think you still might need a PopSocket at times, or you just aren’t ready to give it up, the brand now makes a slimmer version: its Low-Pro Grip . There are other competitors, like the OhSnap grips , which aren’t a bad alternative either.

There’s something about the Duo that seems to have kicked off a new iPhone personalization trend, at least judging by what I’ve been seeing on social media.

Unlike a regular iPhone, where every phone case is simply a shell that offers a degree of protection based on the materials used, the Duo case lineup provides far more variety.

You can buy cases with and without built-in screen protectors, and some use adhesive to better stick to the outer screen, while others don’t. Some cases let you customize the band around the outer screen with a different color than the case that protects the rest of the phone.

Then you have cases that cover the hinge, while others leave it exposed. There are cases that offer holes where you can attach straps, wristlets, and charms. Some of those have attachment points at the bottom and others on the side.

Essentially, there are a lot of options for customizing how you want to carry the Duo and how you want to express your own style.

I’m also now starting to see whimsical cases that come with attached pens . (Thank goodness — most of the pen cases so far have been kind of plain!)

I also believe there’s something about the Duo that particularly appeals to women. Maybe because it’s small, or maybe it’s because you can attach a strap to its side and carry it like a little purse. Or maybe because, like a purse, you can deck it out with chains and charms — a choice that’s grown increasingly popular as young people have embraced whimsical, retro tech as a way to express their individuality and sense of fashion.

The Duo easily lends itself to this trend, perhaps even more than a regular iPhone. It becomes an accessory you want on display, not one buried in a bag.

Before switching to the Duo, I spent a lot of time thinking about what I’d be giving up by moving away from the Pro Max.

I’m surprised to find that, a month later, I only think about what I’d have to give up if I switched back to a traditional iPhone. It’s not just the extra space of the unfolded screen I’d miss — it’s all the little habits I’ve developed around having different screen sizes for different purposes.

The Duo makes me pause and think about how I want to use an app. That small moment of deliberation, before I even open the phone, has helped me break some of my more mindless smartphone habits, particularly around social media.

That’s not a benefit I could have anticipated if I’d judged the device by its specifications alone.

news.title: MacBook Neo vs MacBook Air: Which should you buy right now?
news.summary: Apple’s Mac lineup is stronger than ever this year, largely thanks to the new MacBook Neo. If you’re deciding between the MacBook Neo and the MacBook Air this holiday season, here’s everything you need to know. MacBook Neo 256GB: $599 (Reg. $699) MacBook Neo 512GB with Touch ID: $699 (Reg. $799) 13-inch M5 MacBook Air: Up to $400 off 15-inch M5 MacBook Air: Up to $400 off more…
news.body:
Apple’s Mac lineup is stronger than ever this year, largely thanks to the new MacBook Neo. If you’re deciding between the MacBook Neo and the MacBook Air this holiday season, here’s everything you need to know.

The MacBook Neo is Apple’s most affordable laptop ever, starting at $699 (currently on sale for $599 ). It features a solid aluminum design that comes in a range of fun colors, including Silver, Blush, Citrus, and Indigo

Unlike Apple’s other Macs, the MacBook Neo is powered by an A-series chip rather than an M-series chip. It uses the A18 Pro chip originally introduced with the iPhone 16 Pro, featuring a 6-core CPU and 5-core GPU.

The MacBook Neo comes with 8GB of unified memory, with no additional RAM configuration options available. It starts with 256GB of storage, with a 512GB configuration available for an additional $100 . That $100 upgrade also gets you Touch ID, which is not included in the base model.

There are some other trade-offs compared to the MacBook Air. The MacBook Neo lacks a backlit keyboard, MagSafe charging, and a Force Touch trackpad. It also has more limited USB-C connectivity and supports just one external display.

Still, the MacBook Neo offers an impressive feature set. It has a 13-inch display, up to 16 hours of battery life, a 1080p FaceTime camera, and the full macOS experience.

The MacBook Air, meanwhile, was updated earlier this year with Apple’s M5 chip. It starts at $1,299 , making it $600 more expensive than the entry-level MacBook Air. The MacBook Air is currently on sale with a starting price of $999 .

For that $600 upgrade, the MacBook Air offers several key advantages over the MacBook Air. The M5 chip has a 10-core CPU and up to a 10-core GPU, enabling better sustained performance than the MacBook Neo.

The MacBook Air also starts with 16GB of unified memory and 512GB of storage, both double the entry-level MacBook Neo. You can configure it with up to 32GB of memory and 4TB of storage, while the MacBook Neo is limited to 8GB of memory and 512GB of storage.

Apple rates the MacBook Air for up to 18 hours of video streaming and 15 hours of wireless web browsing, compared to 16 hours and 11 hours, respectively, for the MacBook Neo.

Buy MacBook Air:

As I wrote in my review earlier this year, I think the MacBook Neo is a great Mac, full stop … not just because of the great price. It can handle the vast majority of things most people will throw at it. This includes web browsing, basic photo and video editing, research, and much more.

The M5 MacBook Air, meanwhile, offers more power and more configuration options. This makes it a great option for people who need more storage, RAM, and power than the MacBook Neo can offer.

One of my favorite things about the MacBook Air is that it’s available in two screen sizes. The 15-inch MacBook Air is one of my favorite Apple laptops with a combination of the ultra-thin and light design and the larger screen. I think a lot of people forget it exists, but it’s an excellent choice.

To recap, I think the MacBook Neo is a great choice for everyday tasks like web browsing, email, writing, and streaming. The MacBook Air is a better fit for more demanding workflows, including photo and video editing, coding, working with large spreadsheets, and heavy multitasking.

Beyond performance, the MacBook Air offers a handful of niceties that you won’t find on the MacBook Neo. These include a backlit keyboard, a larger display with True Tone, MagSafe charging, a better webcam and speakers, and a Force Touch trackpad. It also includes Touch ID on every configuration, longer battery life, and support for two external displays.

If it’s in the budget, I think the MacBook Air is an excellent choice for all Mac shoppers. It’s plenty powerful, thin and light, and is highly configurable compared to the MacBook Neo.

What do you think of the MacBook Neo vs MacBook Air decision? Which would you choose? Let us know down in the comments.

news.title: Man sentenced to 47 months in prison after using AI to impersonate streamer N3on
news.summary: David Anthony Sanchez, the man who impersonated N3on, scammed victims out of $260,000 worth of cryptocurrency.
news.body:
David Anthony Sanchez scammed victims out of $260,000 worth of cryptocurrency.

A Florida man who is known as "Dave the Jewler" has been sentenced to 47 months in prison after running a cryptocurrency scam that involved using AI to impersonate a well-known streamer. David Anthony Sanchez, who pleaded guilty to money laundering and aggravated identity theft, was also ordered to pay restitution to the victims.

As spotted by Aftermath , the US Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Florida said Sanchez used AI to clone the voice of Mikyle "N3on" Rafiq in order to convince the people behind a memecoin project that the streamer had agreed to endorse, promote and take part in their scheme. The scammer pretended to be both N3on and the streamer's representative while communicating with the project's organizers.

Sanchez fooled them into transferring around $260,000 worth of cryptocurrency to accounts he controlled. He then converted some of the crypto into US dollars that he used for his personal benefit.

"Behind every fraud scheme are real people who suffer real financial harm," Yara Lorenzo Klukas, acting US Attorney for the Southern District of Florida, said. "In this case, the defendant exploited artificial intelligence to manipulate the trust of unsuspecting victims and deprive them of their money. Today's sentence reflects our commitment to protecting victims, safeguarding the integrity of our financial markets and holding accountable those who exploit emerging technologies to defraud others."

N3on's not exactly a stranger to AI clones of himself, as it happens. Aftermath noted that he tried using a deepfake of himself to keep his Kick stream going around the clock . N3on's likeness was also used in an AI-generated movie that was released a few months ago.

news.title: The Screens app will let you turn your iPhone Duo into an itty bitty MacBook
news.summary: Edovia has updated its Screens remote desktop app with a new Laptop Mode for the iPhone Duo.
news.body:
The app’s latest update will turn half the display into a keyboard for tiny typing.

Edovia's Screens is a remote desktop app, which gives you a way to control your computer for the iPhone, iPad, another Mac or even the Vision Pro. Screens 5.10.6, its latest update, adds the ability to turn your iPhone Duo into a tiny MacBook when it's in a partially open, clamshell configuration. When the phone is folded halfway, you can use the app's new Laptop Mode to display your remote desktop on the upper half of the screen and a keyboard with trackpad below.

Its keyboard supports multiple languages, and you can swipe down on keys to see alternative characters like you can on the iPad. The trackpad supports Screens' gestures. Of course, they're not a complete replacement for actual physical keyboards and trackpads, but they could be good enough to use in a pinch, or even regularly if you're used to typing on a screen or don't need to type anything lengthy.

The iPhone Duo's form factor is so unlike previous iPhones that we'd love to see more fun ways developers can use it to create unique experiences for the device's users. Some developers, however, might not find it that easy: Instagram's Adam Mosseri recently said that it will be "pretty challenging" to design Instagram "in a way that feels great" for the device.

news.title: Gafas eSight Go: potencia visual de 24 aumentos con total libertad de movimiento
news.summary: Las gafas eSight Go son un dispositivo electrónico diseñado para facilitar la percepción de imágenes y detalles del entorno. Están especialmente dirigidas a personas con pérdida de visión central. Su funcionamiento combina una cámara de alta resolución con dos pequeñas pantallas OLED situadas frente a los ojos. A diferencia de unas gafas convencionales, eSight Go […] La entrada Gafas eSight Go: potencia visual de 24 aumentos con total libertad de movimiento se publicó primero en Conticgo .
news.body:
Las gafas eSight Go son un dispositivo electrónico diseñado para facilitar la percepción de imágenes y detalles del entorno.

Están especialmente dirigidas a personas con pérdida de visión central. Su funcionamiento combina una cámara de alta resolución con dos pequeñas pantallas OLED situadas frente a los ojos.

A diferencia de unas gafas convencionales, eSight Go procesa digitalmente las imágenes capturadas y permite modificar su presentación para adaptarla a las necesidades visuales de cada usuario.

El dispositivo incorpora una cámara de alta velocidad que captura imágenes del entorno en tiempo real. A continuación, un sistema de procesamiento digital optimiza la imagen y la reproduce en dos pantallas de alta definición.

De esta manera, el usuario puede visualizar una imagen ampliada y ajustar diferentes parámetros para mejorar su percepción.

Además, las pantallas cuentan con resolución Full HD de 1920 x 1080 píxeles. Esto permite ofrecer imágenes con un buen nivel de detalle y nitidez.

Una de las principales ventajas de estas gafas es la posibilidad de personalizar la experiencia visual. El usuario puede modificar diferentes ajustes dependiendo de la actividad que esté realizando.

Entre sus características destacan:

Hasta 24 aumentos: permite ampliar las imágenes para distinguir detalles que pueden resultar difíciles de percibir.

Enfoque automático: ajusta rápidamente la imagen para mantener la nitidez.

Estabilización de imagen: ayuda a reducir las vibraciones y el movimiento de las imágenes.

Filtros de color y contraste: permiten adaptar la presentación visual a las necesidades de cada persona.

Pantallas OLED Full HD: ofrecen imágenes de alta definición directamente frente a los ojos.

Campo de visión de 45 grados: permite visualizar una zona amplia mientras se conserva la visión periférica natural.

Además, el dispositivo tiene un diseño inalámbrico y ligero. Incorpora una batería ergonómica que se coloca alrededor del cuello y proporciona hasta tres horas de uso continuo.

Las gafas eSight Go están pensadas para facilitar actividades que requieren reconocer detalles o visualizar información a diferentes distancias.

Por ejemplo, pueden ayudar a:

Ver la televisión con mayor claridad.

Leer libros y documentos.

Reconocer rostros.

Consultar pantallas y dispositivos electrónicos.

Observar objetos situados a cierta distancia.

También permiten conservar la visión periférica natural. Esta característica resulta especialmente interesante para las personas que necesitan mantener referencias visuales del entorno mientras utilizan el dispositivo.

No obstante, conservar la visión periférica no significa que las gafas sustituyan otras ayudas de movilidad. Es importante seguir las recomendaciones del fabricante y valorar su uso en diferentes situaciones.

Las eSight Go representan una alternativa dentro de las ayudas electrónicas para la baja visión. Sin embargo, no todas las personas obtienen los mismos resultados.

Su utilidad depende de factores como la patología ocular, el resto visual y las necesidades de cada usuario.

Por eso, antes de adquirir un dispositivo de estas características, es recomendable realizar una valoración individual y comprobar si sus prestaciones se ajustan a las necesidades visuales de la persona.

La tecnología puede ofrecer nuevas oportunidades, pero elegir una ayuda adecuada requiere conocer las características de cada usuario.

news.title: Google search alternative Kagi launches Gmail rival
news.summary: The pitch is an unusual combination of privacy promises and AI features.
news.body:
Kagi, a small, Palo Alto, California-based software company that provides a subscription-based search engine as an alternative to Google, has launched a Gmail-like e-mail service. Dubbed Kagi Mail, it makes many of the same claims as the search engine product: privacy, personal data sovereignty, customization, and control.

Additionally, Kagi is rolling out a calendar as part of the mail service. Right now, both the email and calendar interfaces are web-only, but native Android and iOS apps are planned for the fourth quarter of next year.

The email interface, currently in public beta, is minimalist. It emphasizes keyboard commands, as well as a private and ad-free experience. (You can see more details in Kagi's blog post about what they mean by private.) Other feature offerings include unlimited aliases and domains, an anti-lock-in policy for user data, 50GB of storage, rule-based filtering with Sieve, an MCP server, and several optional, off-by-default AI features, like chatting with an agent to search email history, do large-scale re-labeling, or define additional filtering rules.

news.title: FCC approves SpaceX plan to put AI data centers in space
news.summary: The FCC dismissed some of the key concerns raised by opponents, including potential threats to scientific research, because the agency determined they fell outside its regulatory authority.
news.body:
SpaceX was given conditional approval by the Federal Communications Commission on Wednesday to deploy and operate a constellation of up to 1 million satellites for its orbital data center business, a regulatory victory for Elon Musk and his bid to move AI data centers into space.

The FCC authorization was granted despite objections from Amazon, Viasat, and the American Astronomical Society, which flagged concerns over orbital debris and congestion, radiofrequency interference, and environmental consequences. Amazon, which is building a competitor to SpaceX’s Starlink service, argued in its petition that the application lacked basic details and described it as a “lofty ambition rather than a real plan.” Despite that lack of detail, Amazon also said the proposal “risks real harm.”

The FCC dismissed some of the key concerns raised by opponents, including potential threats to scientific research, because the agency determined they fell outside its regulatory authority.

FCC Chair Brendan Carr said in a statement that the action “opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America’s leadership and growth.”

Musk thanked Carr in a post on X , writing “Much appreciate. This will be a great asset to America and the world.”

This initial regulatory approval doesn’t mean orbital data centers are imminent.

SpaceX faces a number of technical and economic challenges, including how to dramatically reduce the cost of manufacturing and launching satellites, cool processors in space, and even how to secure financing for chips that are destined for orbit.

The company must also clear other regulatory hurdles. The FCC has not yet approved SpaceX’s plans to handle orbital debris for satellites that would operate above 600 kilometers, for instance. SpaceX requested a waiver of existing FCC rules, which requires satellites ending missions below 2,000 kilometers reenter Earth’s atmosphere within five years of completing those missions. The company is interested in moving some of these retired satellites into other orbits around Earth or even around the sun, according to the FCC authorization document .

SpaceX has said it plans to deploy the satellites, known as Starmind, at altitudes ranging from 500 to 1,002 kilometers. The FCC’s approval gives SpaceX the authority to use radiofrequency communications to maintain contact with and control its orbital data centers from Earth if their primary communications systems fail. The Starmind satellites would primarily communicate using lasers to connect with other satellites, including SpaceX’s Starlink.

The FCC has given SpaceX time to sort out these issues. Under the approval, SpaceX has seven years to get its first operational satellite into orbit and 14 years to deploy the entire constellation.

news.title: Ladybird browser's first downloadable alpha is surprisingly capable
news.summary: An independent browser engine arrives on Linux and macOS, and we've tried it.
news.body:
Note: At the time of writing, I was unaware of criticism directed at Ladybird creator Andreas Kling’s public statements. Readers interested in this background can find further context in accounts by Kelson Vibber and Drew DeVault .

After four years of work to build a browser engine from scratch, the Ladybird project released its first downloadable alpha on November 23, offering prebuilt versions for macOS and Linux. Previously, curious users had to compile the browser themselves from its source. Now it's an installable package with automatic updating.

Ladybird is most notable for what it isn't: another browser fork. Where Chrome, Edge, Brave, and Opera all run on Google's Blink engine, and Firefox depends on Gecko, Ladybird's rendering engine and its LibJS JavaScript engine were written from scratch. "The engine is our own, built from the ground up, and not a fork," project lead Andreas Kling wrote in Monday's announcement. "The browser around it is modest, but functional."

news.title: Etsy clarifies AI terms after seller backlash
news.summary: One veteran illustrator dismisses revisions as "sugar coating."
news.body:
After backlash from sellers frustrated by Etsy’s new AI policies, which appeared to allow the company to train AI on user artwork, Etsy has now clarified its stance.

In a note published on Monday, CEO Kruti Patel Goyal discussed recent tweaks to the company's terms of service and admitted that her team "should’ve given you more context on what the updates meant for your creative content."

“Our recent terms update was meant to reflect the evolving technologies we're using to build better tools and experiences for sellers and the Etsy community,” Goyal wrote this week. “It was not meant to enable us to train AI models for the purpose of creating copycats of your items. We do not and will not do that.”

news.title: Actualización de software y APP Disponible GOLD 6.1 para iOS y Android: nuevas funciones y mejoras
news.summary: El Centro de Tiflotecnología e Innovación (CTI) presenta la versión 6.1 del Gestor ONCE de Libros Digitales (GOLD) para dispositivos iOS y Android . Esta actualización incorpora nuevas funciones y mejoras para facilitar el uso de la aplicación y la lectura de las obras.
news.body:
El Centro de Tiflotecnología e Innovación (CTI) presenta la versión 6.1 del Gestor ONCE de Libros Digitales (GOLD) para dispositivos iOS y Android . Esta actualización incorpora nuevas funciones y mejoras para facilitar el uso de la aplicación y la lectura de las obras.

Published 25 November 2026 by lciaffoni

Ariadne GPS is an orientation app designed for blind and visually impaired people, available on iPhone since 2011 and now on Android. It tells you where you are and what is around you, and lets you explore the map with your finger.

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

Designed from the start for TalkBack: all buttons are labeled, and the main functions also have TalkBack actions (TalkBack menu > Actions), e.g. Repeat, Places list, Sort by direction/distance, Quick save. On the map you explore directly with one finger (no passthrough); double tap opens the map commands (zoom, move, say the address, add favorite, report); two fingers drag the map; shake or the Close button closes it. On Android 11 and earlier, choosing an action by swiping and double tapping may not run it (a TalkBack limitation); TalkBack menu > Actions always works. Also usable without TalkBack, with its own gestures and visual help; follows system font size and dark theme.

news.title: Gafas Retiplus 2: qué son y cómo ayudan en la baja visión
news.summary: Retiplus 2 son unas gafas inteligentes de realidad aumentada pensadas para personas con baja visión. Quien las usa se pone estas gafas en la cabeza, lleva las manos libres y ve la imagen mejorada a través de sus lentes transparentes. Durante años, las lupas electrónicas obligaban a elegir entre ver con detalle o caminar con […] La entrada Gafas Retiplus 2: qué son y cómo ayudan en la baja visión se publicó primero en Conticgo .
news.body:
Retiplus 2 son unas gafas inteligentes de realidad aumentada pensadas para personas con baja visión. Quien las usa se pone estas gafas en la cabeza, lleva las manos libres y ve la imagen mejorada a través de sus lentes transparentes.

Durante años, las lupas electrónicas obligaban a elegir entre ver con detalle o caminar con seguridad. Hoy, estas gafas permiten aprovechar el resto visual útil en tiempo real sin quedar aislado del entorno.

Retiplus 2 es un sistema español de gafas inteligentes creado junto a oftalmólogos y optometristas. A diferencia de los visores cerrados de realidad virtual, estas gafas son ligeras y transparentes.

El equipo se compone de unas gafas con cámara integrada, lentes transparentes y un pequeño mando de control que va conectado por cable y se lleva en el bolsillo. Su función no es solo ampliar lo que miras, sino adaptar la imagen a la zona sana de cada retina .

Así se reduce el cansancio visual y se evitan mareos al caminar por la calle o por sitios nuevos.

Cada patología ocular daña una parte distinta del campo visual. Por eso, estas gafas se ajustan a medida para distintos perfiles:

DMAE y enfermedad de Stargardt (pérdida de visión central): Las gafas desplazan la imagen frontal hacia la zona sana de la retina que sigue funcionando. Así rodean la mancha ciega central.

Glaucoma avanzado y retinosis pigmentaria (visión en túnel): El sistema reúne una escena amplia dentro del ángulo central que conserva la persona. De este modo, resulta más fácil notar escalones, puertas o gente a los lados sin mover la cabeza sin parar.

Retinopatía diabética: Mejoran el contraste y marcan los bordes de los objetos. Esto ayuda a distinguir cosas sobre fondos complejos, como un vaso transparente sobre un mantel claro.

Llevar estas gafas de realidad aumentada en el día a día aporta ventajas claras frente a otras ayudas ópticas:

Ves a la vez lo real y la ayuda digital: Al mirar por lentes transparentes, mantienes tu noción del espacio y recibes apoyo visual encima.

Manos libres fuera de casa: Puedes caminar, comprar, mirar carteles o reconocer caras a media distancia sin sujetar lupas.

Modos listos para cada momento: El especialista guarda ajustes para leer, andar por casa, salir a la calle o ver la tele, y cambias entre ellos con un botón.

Aunque los resultados clínicos son favorables, usar las gafas Retiplus 2 exige un proceso guiado:

Hace falta resto visual: No sirven si hay ceguera total. La persona debe conservar algo de visión útil para entender lo que muestran las lentes.

Ajuste en óptica o clínica: Un óptico-optometrista de baja visión debe revisar tu campo visual y configurar las gafas para ti.

Tiempo de adaptación: El cerebro suele necesitar entre dos y seis semanas de práctica para acostumbrarse a ver la imagen ajustada mientras te mueves.

Si quieres ver otras gafas parecidas dentro de esta categoría, estas dos opciones son habituales en baja visión:

Gafas eSight Go: Llevan pantallas internas de alta definición con hasta 24 aumentos y enfoque rápido, pensadas sobre todo para ver la tele, pantallas o pizarras sin perder la visión de abajo y los lados para andar.

Gafas Oxsight Onyx: Están orientadas a quienes han perdido visión lateral. Resaltan contornos de personas y obstáculos con colores vivos dentro de la zona central útil.

Las gafas Retiplus 2 acercan la realidad aumentada a la vida diaria de quienes tienen baja visión. Al ajustarse a la vista de cada persona, ayudan a moverse con más seguridad y a mantener la autonomía dentro y fuera de casa.

news.title: BusNeighbor
news.summary: BusNeighbor shows the live positions of SEPTA buses and trolleys in Philadelphia and the surrounding counties, refreshed every 30 seconds. It is free, with no…
news.body:
Published 24 November 2026 by BusNeighborDev

BusNeighbor shows the live positions of SEPTA buses and trolleys in Philadelphia and the surrounding counties, refreshed every 30 seconds. It is free, with no ads, no accounts, and no tracking. Location is optional, and the app never asks for it when it starts.

If you ride SEPTA buses or trolleys, you know the question: where is my bus right now, and is it coming down my street or detoured around the block? I built a free app called BusNeighbor that answers that question with VoiceOver and TalkBack. I made BusNeighbor because I needed a super-clear map I could read quickly so I’d never miss a bus. When I met a friend with low vision, I realized how an easy-to-read map could help him, too.

BusNeighbor is not affiliated with SEPTA. It uses SEPTA’s public data. Search for BusNeighbor in the App Store or Google Play, or visit bus.dydx.org. Questions and bug reports are welcome at bu * @ ** dx.org .

Accessibility and User Comments:

Here is one way to use it: checking on your bus from home before you walk to the stop.

1. Choose the routes you ride. Double-tap the large Actions Menu button near the bottom of the screen, then choose Add/Remove Buses. Under "Choose your routes for display," double-tap each route you ride, then close the list. The app keeps those routes in view.

2. Turn on the list of nearby vehicles. It is off by default, so you only do this once: double-tap Accessibility Settings at the top of the screen (the eye button) and turn on Closest Vehicles Readout. A list called Closest Vehicles then appears at the bottom of the map. Each bus is read as its route, nearest intersection, and distance.

3. Find out where a bus is headed next. Double-tap a bus on the map to open its details. BusNeighbor names the next stop it will serve. If the bus is off its regular route, it says "On a detour now." If buses are skipping stops on the road ahead, it names the stops being skipped. Before you head out, you'll know whether the bus is really coming to your stop.

4. Listen for the data age. The app tells you how old its information is, and a bus that has stopped reporting is marked differently from a live one, so you won't wait for a bus that isn't coming.

Detours: When SEPTA detours a route, BusNeighbor shows a detour card that lists, turn by turn, the streets buses take instead, and says whether the detour is in effect. It also marks where recent buses actually went.

Low vision: There are twelve contrast-tuned map color schemes and support for large text. Each route you pick is drawn in its own color, under the street names.

Sharing: An instructor or family member can send a link, or print a QR code, that opens BusNeighbor with a set of routes already chosen.

Last Tested App version and Android version:

1.1.8. Android 17

It’s built around an inbox for new episodes and queues for what you’re listening to. Audio & Playback Tripod has integrated EQ settings, can trim silence, and balance audio levels across episodes, for the smoothest listening experience. You can skip chapters or use the transcript to jump to a specific line. It also has an innovative playback scrubber that snaps to the starts of chapters, glides over skipped chapters, and uses haptic feedback for extra precision. Inbox The inbox is where new episodes arrive and you can decide whether to keep or ignore episodes. For the shows where you listen to every episode, you can send them straight to the queue. Queues Instead of playlists you have to manually manage, Tripod has automatic queues. There’s a main queue, favourites, shorts, in-progress, and each genre gets its own queue. news.title: RayNeo iO: unas gafas inteligentes con inteligencia artificial que proyectan información directamente en el campo visual
news.summary: Las nuevas gafas de RayNeo incorporan una pantalla MicroLED transparente, traducción en tiempo real y asistencia mediante inteligencia artificial. Cada vez son más los fabricantes que incorporan pantallas, asistentes de inteligencia artificial y nuevas funciones para facilitar el acceso a la información en el día a día. Uno de los últimos lanzamientos en este ámbito […] La entrada RayNeo iO: unas gafas inteligentes con inteligencia artificial que proyectan información directamente en el campo visual se publicó primero en Conticgo .
news.body:
Las nuevas gafas de RayNeo incorporan una pantalla MicroLED transparente, traducción en tiempo real y asistencia mediante inteligencia artificial.

Cada vez son más los fabricantes que incorporan pantallas, asistentes de inteligencia artificial y nuevas funciones para facilitar el acceso a la información en el día a día. Uno de los últimos lanzamientos en este ámbito son las RayNeo iO , unas gafas inteligentes que apuestan por integrar una pequeña pantalla directamente en el campo visual del usuario.

Las RayNeo iO incorporan una pantalla MicroLED binocular que proyecta información en color verde directamente delante de los ojos. Según el fabricante, esta pantalla ofrece una experiencia equivalente a contemplar una pantalla virtual de 33 pulgadas.

Uno de sus aspectos más destacados es su transparencia del 97 %, que permite mantener una visión amplia del entorno mientras se consulta la información proyectada.

Con un peso de apenas 33 gramos, las gafas están diseñadas para utilizarse durante buena parte del día. También cuentan con un brillo máximo de 1.300 nits y una batería que, según RayNeo, puede alcanzar las 48 horas de uso habitual.

Entre sus principales funciones encontramos la traducción simultánea y los subtítulos que aparecen directamente en el campo visual.

También incorporan un asistente de inteligencia artificial al que se puede acceder mediante comandos de voz. Esta herramienta permite consultar información, recibir respuestas y gestionar diferentes tareas cotidianas.

Las gafas también permiten consultar notificaciones y otros datos sin necesidad de sacar el teléfono móvil.

Aunque algunas de sus características podrían resultar interesantes para determinados usuarios con discapacidad visual, es importante analizar sus limitaciones.

La pantalla integrada podría facilitar el acceso a información digital a personas que conservan suficiente resto visual para distinguir los elementos proyectados.

No cuentan con cámara, por lo que no pueden utilizarse para reconocer objetos, leer textos del entorno mediante OCR o describir escenas. Su pantalla es monocromática y no consta que permita adaptar la información mediante herramientas específicas de accesibilidad, como la inversión de colores o la modificación del contraste.

Aunque pueden ofrecer algunas ventajas a usuarios con determinadas necesidades visuales, no es un dispositivo diseñado específicamente para personas con baja visión.

Las RayNeo iO representan un nuevo paso en la integración de la inteligencia artificial y las pantallas transparentes en dispositivos de uso cotidiano.

No obstante, su utilidad para las personas con discapacidad visual dependerá de las características de cada usuario y de su capacidad para percibir la información proyectada.

La tecnología accesible no consiste únicamente en incorporar inteligencia artificial o pantallas a nuevos dispositivos. También requiere diseñar herramientas que respondan a las necesidades reales de las personas con discapacidad visual.

Si te ha gustado esta noticia no te pierdas las últimas novedades en tiflotectnología en nuestro apartado de noticias y redes sociales .

Fuente: Web oficil RayNeo

news.title: Tact: Find It by Touch
news.summary: A haptic game you play by touch, without looking at the screen. The screen is black glass. Feel for the one place that is different, and break it. Tap anywhere with one to five fingers, the way you'd play a piano. Each tap answers with a small tick under your fingertip. Somewhere, one place feels different: a little longer, a double tap, or a little harder. When you find it, keep tapping it. A crack runs across the glass, and it breaks, with a deep haptic, a short high glass sound and a soft light. Play it absent-mindedly, with the TV on. Each pane you break still feels like a small win. While you play, no score appears on screen. Numbers show only when you pause, when a Time Attack run ends, or when a pane breaks in a Duel. FOUR WAYS TO PLAY • Calm: No time limit, no score. Find the one place that feels different, and keep breaking the glass • Standard: Each pane you break makes the difference a little subtler (12 levels). If you can't find it, it becomes clearer again. Pause to see your current level and your best • Time Attack: How many panes can you break while the line goes once around the screen in 60 seconds? Cues at the start, every 15 seconds and in the last 3 seconds. Your best is kept • Duel: Two players, one iPhone laid between you, face to face. Each of you has a place of your own that feels different (longer or double tap). Whoever's place breaks first scores, even if the other player broke it. First to 1, 3, 5 or 7 RECORDS • Your best level in Standard and your best count in Time Attack • Records made with Stronger Difference or Sound Hints on are kept apart as assisted records MAKE IT YOURS • Haptic Strength: Gentle, Standard or Strong • Sound volume, and Tap Sound • Touch Trace, and Completion Light (Off, Soft or Bright) • Taps to Break: 5, 7, 10 or 12 (10 to start) • Settings are under the faint gear that appears at the top right when you pause. While playing, hold two fingers for two seconds, then lift them GETTING STARTED • On first launch, a short tutorial of about 30 seconds, on a bigger 2×3 grid • Watch it again any time with Replay Tutorial in Settings FOR EVERYONE • Playable with VoiceOver. The play area takes your taps directly, and the tutorial text, the time left and results in Time Attack, level changes, and points and wins in a Duel are read aloud • Stronger Difference makes the difference clearer and uses only the two clearest kinds • With Sound Hints on, the place that feels different also sounds a little different • Reduce Animation makes broken pieces fade where they are instead of falling. Reduce Motion in iOS Settings is respected too • The whole screen never flashes bright white SOUND • Sounds play along with your music or TV. They don't stop other audio • No sound in Silent Mode. You can play without sound MADE FOR IPHONE HAPTICS • Tact is played by feel, so it is best on iPhone • On devices without haptics, such as iPad, you find the different place by sound (turn the sound on, and turn Silent Mode off) YOURS, ON YOUR IPHONE • No account, and no network connection • Settings and records stay on this iPhone • No ads, no in-app purchases, no tracking Requires an iPhone with iOS 18 or later. Available in English, Japanese, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), Korean, Spanish, French, German and Portuguese (Brazil).

news.title: FantacyCricket
news.summary: FantacyCricket is a full cricket simulation built from the ground up for blind and visually impaired players. Every ball, shot and wicket is played through…
news.body:
Published 21 November 2026 by nila5

FantacyCricket is a full cricket simulation built from the ground up for blind and visually impaired players. Every ball, shot and wicket is played through 3D audio, speech and gestures. Play quick matches or longer formats against the computer, or real-time online one on one matches against real people. Choose your line and length when bowling, read the ball by sound when batting, and play shots in every direction. Developed by Delta Production in Sri Lanka, with over 1,000 players.

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

Designed for screen reader users from day one, not adapted later. Fully playable with TalkBack: every button and menu item is labelled, and all game events are spoken.

Gameplay uses audio cues and swipe gestures, and menus never close on their own. An in-app guide explains every gesture and feature. Tested by blind players with TalkBack. Developer contact: deltaproduction14@gmail.com

news.title: Sonnounce
news.summary: Sonnounce lets you send spoken announcements from your phone to your Sonos speakers. Hold down a button, say your message, release, and it plays on…
news.body:
Published 20 November 2026 by Flightguy0

Sonnounce lets you send spoken announcements from your phone to your Sonos speakers. Hold down a button, say your message, release, and it plays on the speakers you choose in your own voice. Perfect for telling the family dinner is ready without shouting through the house. It works with all Sonos speakers, including older S1 systems, and includes noise reduction. Sonnounce also works with Homey and Home Assistant, so you can send announcements to your speakers at home even when you are away. Sonnounce is completely free.

Homey: https://homey.app/a/dk.hoffmeyer-net.sonosannouncements Home Assistant: https://github.com/Flightguy0/sonnounce

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

I am the developer, and I am blind myself. Sonnounce was built and tested with a screen reader from day one, and I use it daily with TalkBack. All buttons are labelled, and the main announce button works with a standard TalkBack double tap and hold.

Feedback from other TalkBack users is very welcome at flyveradio@flyveradio.dk
